name: dotnet-testing-filesystem-testing-abstractions

Test file and directory operations with `System.IO.Abstractions`, `IFileSystem`, and `MockFileSystem`; use for refactoring static `System.IO` code, unit tests, filesystem-state simulation, IO exception scenarios, and testable file-processing services. Static `System.IO` makes tests slower (disk IO is 10-100x slower than memory), environment-dependent, side-effect-prone, race-prone, and difficult to test for errors.

Core interfaces: `IFileSystem` exposes `IFile`, `IDirectory`, `IFileInfo`, `IDirectoryInfo`, `IPath`, `IDriveInfo`.

Packages:
<PackageReference Include="System.IO.Abstractions" Version="21.*" />
<PackageReference Include="System.IO.Abstractions.TestingHelpers" Version="21.*" />

Inject `IFileSystem`; replace `File.ReadAllText(path)` with `_fileSystem.File.ReadAllText(path)`. Register:
services.AddSingleton<IFileSystem, FileSystem>();
services.AddScoped<ConfigService>();

Tests: use a fresh `MockFileSystem` per test, seeded via `new MockFileSystem(new Dictionary<string, MockFileData> { ["config.json"] = new MockFileData("{ \"key\": \"value\" }") })`. Assert reads, writes, copies, file info, backups, and line counts against mock state. Mock directories with `MockDirectoryData`. For exceptions MockFileSystem support is limited; use NSubstitute (`Substitute.For<IFileSystem>()`, `Substitute.For<IFile>()`) to make reads throw `UnauthorizedAccessException`.

Use `_fileSystem.Path.Combine("configs", "app.json")`; check `_fileSystem.File.Exists(filePath)`; create missing parent directories with `Path.GetDirectoryName` and `Directory.CreateDirectory`. Handle `UnauthorizedAccessException`, `IOException`, and `DirectoryNotFoundException`. Verify independent mock state for every test.

Hardcode path separators:
"// ❌ Don't do this" — do not use `"configs\\app.json"` or `"configs/app.json"`; use `Path.Combine`.

Use real file system in unit tests:
"// ❌ This is not a unit test" — use `MockFileSystem`, not `new FileSystem()`.

Ignore exception handling:
"// ❌ Don't assume file always exists" — check existence and handle exceptions.

Only create files necessary for testing
Avoid simulating oversized files in tests
